articles.title: She gets 16 pelvic exams a day – so yours don’t hurt
articles.summary: Molly Callahan, a gynecological teaching assistant, helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams. On her busiest days, Molly Callahan, has 16 speculums inserted into her vagina.
body: It’s not as unpleasant as you might think. In fact, the point is to help students learn how to do it without causing discomfort. Contrary to common belief, pap smears – tests that screen for cervical cancer – don’t have to be painful.

Pap smears have reduced cervical cancer–related deaths by 86%, but many women avoid them due to confusion around guidelines, perceived lack of symptoms and, most commonly, speculum discomfort and embarrassment. One large study of US cancer statistics data found that from 2005 to 2023, 32% of women aged 21-29, and 15% of women aged 30-65, had never had a pap smear.

The negative association isn’t surprising. Looking at the cervix for indications of cancer became more common in the early 20th century, said Dr Kirsten Gardner, director of medical humanities at the University of Texas San Antonio, and methods centered innovation over comfort.

articles.title: Branding it like Beckham: how Jude Bellingham is future-proofing his fame
articles.summary: From Calvin Klein to British Vogue, the Real Madrid man is leading the way when it comes to football’s foray into fashion. But is he playing it safe? This Sunday, Jude Bellingham will line up with his England teammates for a match against Spain.
body: It’s a savvy move for the 23-year-old, future-proofing himself as a power player both on and off the pitch. This is a roadmap carved out by David Beckham, who since retiring in 2013 has become a brand and personality that transcends sport. Beckham – together with his wife, Victoria – became a billionaire this year.

The Calvin Klein ads, which feature Bellingham in underwear, sometimes in his signature Christ the Redeemer pose, have caused a stir since appearing in London and New York, with passersby stopping to take selfies. The popularity of a billboard in Soho, New York also cements his celebrity status in the US after this summer’s World Cup.

Of course Bellingham is a bona fide star on the pitch. Mark Borkowski, a public relations consultant, says this factor is pivotal to the footballer’s crossover appeal. “Bellingham is an exceptional sporting talent, and his brand value is understandably enormous,” he says. “But fashion doesn’t create that value, football does. Fashion merely provides another means of exploiting it.”

articles.title: Kennedy’s Future: Will Democrats Try to Impeach Him, or Actually Work With Him?
articles.summary: Most Democrats abhor the health secretary’s stance on vaccines, but some see an opportunity to win voters from his MAHA movement by joining with him on food and environmental issues.
body: Sheryl Gay Stolberg covers Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his MAHA movement.

Three days after last week’s “blue wave” election, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. posted a warning on X to anyone suspecting his Make America Healthy Again movement had been weakened. “It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” he wrote.

The phrase, a reference to the 1981 movie “Clash of the Titans” that gained currency in 2020 among far-right internet personalities who claimed Democrats stole the election, suggests Mr. Kennedy will fight for his agenda and has no intention of leaving his job despite the defeat of several MAHA-backed candidates.
The question now is whether Democrats will use their new majorities in Congress to try to push him out.

articles.title: Marlon Brando cool to Jensen Huang joke: how the black leather jacket became a meme
articles.summary: Once the ultimate symbol of Hollywood rebellion, the former Nvidia chief’s signature look is now being mocked as a midlife crisis cliche. For nearly two decades a black leather jacket has been a key part of Jensen Huang’s look. Now it has become a punchline.
body: As the founder and chief executive of Nvidia resigned this week after reports of multiple affairs, his affinity for a leather jacket, an item of clothing typically associated with a man in midlife crisis mode, has become widely mocked.

The Cut ran a story suggesting a clear line between his penchant for a luxury leather jacket and his extramarital affairs. “Jensen Huang’s leather jackets confessed before he did” read the headline. Writing in the New York Times, the author Anand Giridharadas asked “is an expensive leather jacket on a middle-aged man the new symbol of a honeypot victim?”

Meanwhile, the internet is rife with memes, including an AI-generated image of a leather jacket flying at half mast outside Elon Musk’s rocket company SpaceX. There was also another fake image, this time of Huang in a studded leather jacket, that many people believed was real.

Elsewhere, there are plenty of divorced dad jokes doing the rounds. “Jensen leather jacket discourse reminds me of the time two years ago when I wore my beloved moto jacket to a party and my good friend said “great jacket, sorry you got divorced”, wrote one user on X.

articles.title: FKA Twigs’s Josephine Baker Transformation Is Already a Beauty Spectacle
articles.summary: A first look at forthcoming Josephine Baker biopic sees FKA twigs embrace all the vintage beauty signatures of the iconic singer, dancer, and civil rights activist.
body: With lacquered curls spiraling across her forehead, a dark and smoky gaze, and a megawatt smile, FKA twigs has all but disappeared into Josephine Baker. The first image of the British musician as the legendary entertainer in the forthcoming biopic Josephine Baker has arrived, and if this is anything to go by, we’re in for an on-screen beauty transformation for the ages.

In the image, twigs stands atop a dining table, twisting into a playful pose in a pink, crystal-strewn flapper dress with delicate beading and fringe. But it’s the beauty that really transports us to 1920s Paris. Her hair has been molded into an ultra-glossy, close-cropped style, with elaborate kiss curls arranged across her forehead and temples. Her eyes are rimmed with smoldering shadow, her brows sharply defined, and her lips painted a rich red. It’s classic Baker, down to the mischievous expression.

articles.title: Microsoft Officially Apologized for Yesterday's Outages
articles.summary: If you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime.
body: Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major issue somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still showed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

While the root cause of the issue was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the company, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions."

Microsoft says it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The company says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

articles.title: MoMA and Chanel Rolled Out the Red Carpet to Honor Steven Spielberg
articles.summary: It was a night full of unscripted surprises and picture-perfect moments at the Museum of Modern Art’s 18th annual Film Benefit on Thursday—fitting for an evening dedicated to the power of cinema.
body: As the lights dimmed, the crowd marveled as a montage showed the momentous filmography of this year’s honoree, Steven Spielberg: Jaws, Indiana Jones, West Side Story, Jurassic Park, Lincoln, and Minority Report, to name a few. Once the room was illuminated again, there was a collective gasp as the spotlight shone on Tom Cruise, one of the few names who wasn’t initially on the tip sheet for the occasion.

The actor recalled the formative and inspiring experience of watching Jaws for the first time, and cracked jokes about the less-than-desirable jobs he took solely to afford tickets to see Spielberg’s movies at the cinema. Cruise thanked the legendary director for “always being generous to [me] in films, but also being generous to [me] at home” as he, quite literally, jumped off the stage and beelined to his friend and longtime collaborator in the audience to share a long hug.

articles.title: Dua Lipa Has Already Got Her Hands on Winter’s Next It Coat
articles.summary: Offering a sneak peek at Charlotte Simone’s forthcoming collection, Dua Lipa lets the fabulous coat do all the talking.
body: There is a certain kind of winter coat that’s popular right now. Dua Lipa, a longtime devotee of the fabulous, fantastical coat, understands this better than most. It’s one that requires very little else of its wearer. No elaborate styling or carefully coordinated separates needed. Just throw it on over a pair of jeans, and you're dressed. The coat is the outfit!

And so the singer has offered a first look at a yet-to-be-released piece from London-based designer Charlotte Simone ’s forthcoming Winter Drop 2. The jacket features an enormous, shaggy brown collar, extravagant furry cuffs, and a cropped silhouette. Lipa wore hers with faded blue Icon Denim Didy jeans and a black Bottega Veneta Madison shoulder bag, allowing the outerwear to take center stage.

“Dua is a dream girl,” Simone tells Vogue. "She never looks overdone or precious about what she’s wearing. She’ll throw one of our coats over a simple pair of jeans or a slip dress, and suddenly the coat is the whole look. That’s exactly how I design… I want every style to be the statement, the piece that makes you feel instantly put together the moment you step out the door.”

articles.title: How a Trip to India Helped Me Find Peace With a Life-Changing Diagnosis
articles.summary: After over 20 surgeries and some near-death experiences, I had somehow worked up the courage to travel and live my life again.
body: The tuk-tuk ride up the Chamundi Hills near Mysuru, India, took about half an hour. My husband, brother-in-law, and some of my colleagues were split between two rickshaws, winding our way up a massive hill toward the Chamundeshwari Temple. I used to love taking tuk-tuks as a kid, but at age 41 I found that the ride felt like so much more than a fun adventure.

Since childhood I’ve experienced a lot of what doctors call extraintestinal manifestations, which are symptoms that occur when an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) affects parts of the body outside the gut. I dealt with issues like severe joint pain and eye issues alongside constipation and GERD, but at the time doctors didn’t think to refer me to a gastroenterologist. The discomfort and unpredictability of my condition meant I was always scared to travel, even if it was just a road trip.

articles.title: Hugo Boss CEO Daniel Grieder Steps Down Amid Frasers Takeover
articles.summary: Following disappointing Q3 results and the Frasers takeover, Hugo Boss CEO Daniel Grieder has stepped down. Frasers Group’s chief brand partnerships officer David Epstein will succeed the executive.
body: Hugo Boss has announced that CEO Daniel Grieder will depart the German company, effective December 31. David Epstein — currently the chief brand partnerships officer at Frasers Group — will replace him, effective January 1, 2027.

Grieder was appointed CEO in June 2021, overseeing the company’s Claim 5 turnaround — a strategy focused on improving brand relevance, product innovation, digital output, omnichannel experience, and operational logistics to drive growth. Before Hugo Boss, Grieder spent more than 20 years at Tommy Hilfiger.

His mandate at Hugo Boss was to double company sales to €4 billion by 2025, believing the company had lost its relevance within the fashion space. He decided that while the brand’s heritage remained strong, it needed reframing. In 2022, he divided the parent company into two individual brands: Hugo and Boss — positioning Hugo for Gen Z and Boss for millennials.
Grieder also ushered in an ongoing collaboration with David Beckham, introduced in 2025 as a co-designed capsule. For fiscal 2025, Hugo Boss reported €4.3 billion in group sales.
